sci-repo-y10-aran-2014-phys1-mc-1.title: Year 10 Science — Forces, work, energy and power (original source MC)
sci-repo-y10-aran-2014-phys1-mc-1.coverage: Original assessment questions with source figures. Written parts remain in the bank with marks and parent context. Review-required items excluded from automatic battles.

questions.prompt: The unit used to measure ‘power’ is:
A stretched spring stores energy as:
A gun is fired and when the bullet shoots out of the barrel the gun ‘kicks’ back (recoils) in  the person’s hand. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: A: Newton’s third law;forces act on bullet and gun in opposite directions.

questions.prompt: Select the correct statement regarding the Law of Conservation of Energy.
options: The amount of energy increases as it changes from one form to another.
When energy is transferred it always creates sound energy.
Energy may be transferred but is never created or destroyed.
questions.explanation: D: energy can transfer or transform but total energy is conserved.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct definition for ‘elastic potential energy’.
options: Energy stored when an object is raised above the ground.
Energy that is moving as an objects falls.
Energy that is moving as a spring is expanding outwards.
Energy stored in a stretched or compressed material.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct definition for ‘potential energy’.
options: Energy found in moving light energy.
Energy found in moving sound waves

questions.prompt: Choose the correct definition for ‘kinetic energy’.
options: Energy that is stored in chemicals.
Energy that is stored in a stretched object.
The energy of a moving object.
The energy stored in a litre of fuel.
The rate at which work is done.
The amount of energy in an object.
The objects ability to do work.
questions.explanation: A: work done per unit time.

questions.prompt: The equation for work done is W = F x d. The work done on a crate that is pulled 150cm by a force of 200N is:

options: Rate at which work is done.
The mass of a moving object.
Energy transferred by a force that acts over a certain distance.
questions.explanation: C: energy transferred by a force acting through a displacement.

questions.prompt: The equation for work done is W = F x d. The work done on a box that is shifted 2m by a  force of 300N is:
Select the object that does not use elastic potential energy to do work.
options: A ball raised 5m above the ground.
questions.explanation: C: raised ball stores gravitational potential energy.

questions.prompt: The units to measure ‘work done’ is:
Who was known as the ‘Father of Modern Science’?
questions.explanation: A: Galileo Galilei is commonly described by this title.

questions.prompt: The equation for gravitational potential energy is Ep=mgh (remember acceleration due to  gravity is always 9.8m/s2). Abbee has a mass of 40kg and sits on the edge of a 3m high platform. Which of the following would be her gravitational potential energy?

options: Energy cannot be created or destroyed.
The force and object exerts on a fixed area.
The tendency for an object to resist changes in its motion.
questions.explanation: C: resistance to change in velocity.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct definition for ‘gravitational potential energy’.
options: Energy stored in an object when it is above the ground.
Energy stored in a stretched or squashed object.
The rate that a task is accomplished.
questions.explanation: A: energy stored due to elevated position in a gravitational field.
